evals.prompt: I'm the receiving party. Review this NDA and tell me how one-sided it is, then mark up the clauses that hurt us.
evals.expected_output: Fixes perspective to receiving party, scores favorability with rationale, produces a clause-by-clause redline table covering confidentiality/IP/indemnity/liability/jurisdiction, and generates the interactive review HTML.

evals.prompt: Here are my accepted/rejected decisions from the review. Generate the marked-up Word doc as if I commented on it, keeping the counterparty's existing comments.
evals.expected_output: Produces original-format .docx with tracked changes and native comments authored as the user, replies to and resolves overlapping existing comment threads, leaves rejected items untouched, passes validate.py --author.

evals.prompt: Is this SaaS MSA fair to us as the customer? Focus on liability caps, indemnification, SLAs, and data protection, and suggest balanced language for anything off-market.
evals.expected_output: Customer-side analysis; flags one-sided/uncapped liability, one-way indemnity, weak SLAs, missing DPA/breach-notification; proposes balanced fallback language per clause; scores by category.
